churn_resistance.rationale: Good bones: one client module, one config point, per-route URL helpers, typed renderer via documented declaration merging, zero framework internals — an upgrade touches few files. Held back from 5 by the untyped PokeAPI boundary (a data-shape change fails silently at runtime, and the spec explicitly warns data can shift) and small duplications like the triplicated sort-key definitions.

findings.issue: The API boundary is untyped (api<T = any>, any-typed pokemon/species payloads in views/pokemon.tsx:70,77 and data.ts:49), so a change in PokeAPI response shape surfaces as silent runtime undefined/NaN rather than a type error — notable because the spec explicitly warns the data can change.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal response interfaces (species, pokemon, type, move, ability, generation) in api.ts/data.ts and type api<T> call sites; the data already funnels through two modules, so this is a small, high-leverage change.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no timeout or AbortSignal; a hung PokeAPI request stalls the page handler indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Use fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) }) and surface failures as a 502-style error page.

findings.issue: The filter form's hx-target/hx-swap are consumed implicitly by the input and selects; htmx 4 (released 2026-08-28, though 2.x remains npm latest) makes attribute inheritance explicit via :inherited, so this pattern breaks on upgrade.
findings.suggestion: Put hx-target/hx-swap on each triggering element explicitly (or centralize via a documented config), making the views migration-proof when 4.x becomes latest.

findings.issue: The valid sort keys are duplicated in three places: SortKey type (views/pokemon.tsx:29), COLUMNS (:31) and the SORT_KEYS guard in the route.
findings.suggestion: Export COLUMNS (or a derived key list) from views/pokemon.tsx and derive both the SortKey type and the route guard from it.

findings.issue: API URLs are dissected with indexOf('/api/v2/') and a regex instead of the URL API; apiUrl also assumes every absolute URL contains that literal path segment.
findings.suggestion: Use new URL(url).pathname and parse the trailing id from the pathname, which is robust to query strings and base-path changes.

findings.issue: Runtime deps are pinned to exact versions with no caret, so patch and security fixes (e.g. @hono/node-server's 2.1.3 serve-static path-decoding fix) never arrive automatically.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as a reproducibility choice given the lockfile, but prefer ^ ranges with a lockfile and scheduled dependency bumps (e.g. dependabot) for a long-lived app.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache Map is never evicted; it is bounded only incidentally by the API's fixed size.
findings.suggestion: Fine at this scale, but note the bound in a comment or add a simple max-size/TTL eviction so the assumption survives future data growth.

summary: This app is firmly on the current generation: hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5, htmx 2.0.11 and TypeScript 7 are all the latest stable releases (verified against npm/GitHub as of 2026-10-30), the JSX/renderer and node-server idioms match the official skill guidance, and it is structured so a framework upgrade touches few files. The main things that will age poorly are the untyped PokeAPI boundary, a missing upstream fetch timeout, and reliance on htmx 2's implicit attribute inheritance that htmx 4 removes. Overall a forward-looking codebase with a small, well-defined list of hardening items.
